examples.before:
agent:
  prompt: old  # the prompt
  note: x

results.1: exit 0; file gets one quoted line: `prompt: "  indented first\nsecond\n" # the prompt`
results.2: exit 0; file gets one quoted line: `prompt: "  indented first\nsecond\n" # the prompt`
results.3: two arms: exit 0; file gets a block `prompt: |2   # the prompt` / `      indented first` / `    second`. One arm: same quoted line as routes 1 and 2
results.4: exit 0; file gets a block `prompt: |2   # the prompt` / `      indented first` / `    second`

examples.input: `config set agent.note "line one\n  line two\n"` (first line not indented)

results.1: exit 0; file gets a plain block `note: |` / `    line one` / `      line two`, with no `2`
results.3: all arms: exit 0; same plain `note: |` block
two arms: exit 0; file gets `text: |2-` / `          deep` / `      ok`. One arm: file gets `text: "    deep\nok"`

results.1: prints blocks `prompt: |2 …` and `text: |2- …`, even though the file holds quoted strings
results.2: prints the quoted strings, matching the file
results.3: all arms: print blocks `prompt: |2 …` and `text: |2- …`. For the arm that wrote quoted strings, this differs from its file
results.4: prints blocks `prompt: |2 …` and `text: |2- …`, matching the file

results.3: all arms: print `    deep` / `ok`, leading spaces kept

context.in_practice: On every route, `config get` returns the exact value, including leading spaces, and the `# the prompt` comment survives in the file. The difference is how troupe.yml looks. Route 2 and route 1 write the value as one quoted line. Route 4 and two of three arms on route 3 write an indented block marked `|2`. Values whose first line is not indented get an ordinary `|` block on every route. `config show` prints blocks on every route except route 2, so on route 1 (and one arm on route 3) the screen does not match the file.
context.stakes: When a multi-line value starts with spaces, such as an indented prompt, the user either finds it as a readable indented block in troupe.yml or as one quoted line full of `\n`. `config show` may also print it differently from what the file holds. The stored value is the same on every route.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: file and `show` disagree. Route 2: indented values become hard-to-read quoted lines. Routes 3 and 4: readable blocks with a `|2` marker (one arm on route 3 quoted instead).

plan_why: Sets multi-line strings whose first line starts with spaces (top-level mapping and compact list item, with and without a trailing newline) and one that doesn't, so you can see whether the file gets `|2`, a double-quoted scalar, or a plain `|`. Then it reads the values back to check they parse and survive intact.
